Annotate every record in a multi-record fasta

Source: R/annotate.R
annotate_records.Rd

Runs the rRNA anchor caller once over the whole file and ITSx once per strand group, then reconciles per record. Records longer than ITSX_MAX_BP are kept but get anchors only, because ITSx aborts the entire run on an oversized target rather than skipping it.

Usage

annotate_records(fasta, kingdom = "euk", cpu = 2, taxon = "all")

Arguments

fasta

Path to a multi-record fasta.

kingdom

Anchor-caller kingdom.

cpu

Threads for ITSx.

taxon

ITSx -t profile set.

Value

data.frame(seqid, element, type, start, stop, length, strand, model_cov, tool).

Details

barrnap reports coordinates in the input frame; on a genuinely minus-strand record those anchors run 28S -> 5.8S -> 18S in ascending position, the opposite of the ascending order reconcile_features()'s spacer-clipping assumes. ITSx, run on a reverse-complemented copy of those records, reports its regions in the frame where the anchors DO ascend. So minus-strand records are reconciled in that revcomp frame – barrnap's anchors are flipped into it, ITSx's output is used as reported – and the finished model is flipped back to the input frame afterward.
